title: A Spacecraft Uses Earth to Speed Toward Jupiter
summary:
A European spacecraft named Juice just zoomed past Earth. It used our planet's gravity like a slingshot to speed up on its trip to Jupiter. Juice belongs to the European Space Agency, or ESA.

On September 28, Juice flew just 8,640 kilometers above the Indian Ocean. Earth's gravity bent its path by 20 degrees and made it go 3.5 kilometers per second faster. It used very little fuel.

The team made only one small change to Juice's path before the flyby. Saving fuel matters, because Juice will need it later at Jupiter.

The flyby was also practice time. Juice has 10 science tools, and the team tested them by looking at Earth. Juice also flew through Earth's magnetotail, a long tail of our planet's magnetic field.

At Jupiter, Juice will fly past three icy moons, Ganymede, Callisto and Europa, 35 times. It will reach Europa in the early 2030s.
why_it_matters: It shows how scientists use gravity to travel far in space without using much fuel.
